info.bio: Herbert "Herb" Alpert (Los Ángeles (California, EEUU), 31 de marzo de 1935) es un trompetista y cantante estadounidense conocido por formar parte del grupo Herb Alpert & The Tijuana Brass, Herb Alpert's Tijuana Brass o simplemente TJB. También es famoso por ser un ejecutivo de la industria de grabación - él es la letra "A" de A & M Records (un sello de grabación fundado junto a Jerry Moss). Los logros musicales de Alpert cinco números uno, veintiocho álbumes en las listas de Billboard

scenes.name: El pop de papá y mamá
scenes.author: Jon Savage
scenes.desc: Los adultos compraban LPs (a 32 chelines frente a los 6 de un single) y también muchos singles, de modo que la lista británica de 1965 era esquizofrénica: los Stones y los Beatles competían con lo que los adolescentes llamaban «música de papás y mamás», Ken Dodd, los Seekers, los Bachelors o Jim Reeves. La banda sonora de The Sound of Music encabezó la lista de LPs casi todo 1965 y 1966. Los adolescentes más jóvenes encontraban nuevos ídolos como los Walker Brothers, baladistas melodramáticos a lo Spector.

podcast.title: Second Custom Concert Sound System (1965)
podcast.body: In 1965, Herb Alpert and the Tijuana Brass contracted Harry McHughan sound systems for their tour. This initiative is noted as establishing what appears to be the second dedicated concert sound system for touring artists, following The Beach Boys' earlier efforts. "Then, Herb Alpert and the Tijuana Brass contracted Harry McHughan sound systems for their 1965 tour."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Album Arrangement
podcast.body: Quincy Jones arranged albums for Herb Alpert's Tijuana Brass during the 1970s, demonstrating his versatility and continued involvement in producing for various established artists. "He arranged 70's albums for Billy Preston and Herb Alperts Tijuana Brass."

podcast.title: Commissioned Sound System
podcast.body: Herb Alpert and the Tijuana Brass, alongside The Beach Boys, commissioned a specialized sound system for their tours. This initiative was part of a broader trend among popular bands to address the limitations of existing amplification for live music performances in the mid-1960s. "The Beach Boys commissioned a specially built sound system for their tours, so did her bellbird and the Tijuana brass."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

xref.title: Commissioned Sound System
xref.body: The Beach Boys, along with Herb Alpert and the Tijuana Brass, commissioned a specially built sound system for their tours. This move reflected the growing demand for more powerful and effective concert amplification beyond standard PA systems, following issues faced by bands like The Beatles with inadequate volume for large crowds. "The Beach Boys commissioned a specially built sound system for their tours, so did her bellbird and the Tijuana brass."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
